arxiv-1709-09990.title: Computing Treewidth on the GPU
arxiv-1709-09990.creator: Tom C. van der Zanden, Hans L. Bodlaender
arxiv-1709-09990.description: Abstract We present a parallel algorithm for computing the treewidth of a graph on a GPU. We implement this algorithm in OpenCL, and experimentally evaluate its performance. Our algorithm is based on an O ∗ ​ ( 2 n ) O^{*}(2^{n}) -time algorithm that explores the elimination orderings of the graph using a Held-Karp like dynamic programming approach.

arxiv-1901-10068.title: Statistical inference of probabilistic origin-destination demand using day-to-day traffic data
arxiv-1901-10068.creator: Wei Ma, Zhen (Sean) Qian
arxiv-1901-10068.description: Abstract Recent transportation network studies on uncertainty and reliability call for modeling the probabilistic O-D demand and probabilistic network flow. Making the best use of day-to-day traffic data collected over many years, this paper develops a novel theoretical framework for estimating the mean and variance/covariance matrix of O-D demand considering the day-to-day variation induced by travelers’ independent route choices.

arxiv-2109-02710.title: Crash Report Data Analysis for Creating Scenario-Wise, Spatio-Temporal Attention Guidance to Support Computer Vision-based Perception of Fatal Crash Risks
arxiv-2109-02710.creator: Yu Li, Muhammad Monjurul Karim, Ruwen Qin, Zuhui Wang, Zhaozheng Yin, Zeyi Sun
arxiv-2109-02710.description: Abstract 1 Abstract Reducing traffic fatalities and serious injuries is a top priority of the US Department of Transportation. With the rapid development of sensor and Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies, the computer vision (CV)-based crash anticipation in the near-crash phase is receiving growing attention.

arxiv-2112-09333.title: Deep Bayesian Learning for Car Hacking Detection
arxiv-2112-09333.creator: Laha Ale, Scott A. King, Ning Zhang
arxiv-2112-09333.description: Abstract With the rise of self-drive cars and connected-vehicles, cars are equipped with various devices to assistant the drivers or support self-drive systems. Undoubtedly, cars have become more intelligent as we can deploy more and more devices and software on the cars.

arxiv-2204-08167.title: A Study on Prompt-based Few-Shot Learning Methods for Belief State Tracking in Task-oriented Dialog Systems
arxiv-2204-08167.creator: Debjoy Saha, Bishal Santra, Pawan Goyal
arxiv-2204-08167.description: Abstract We tackle the Dialogue Belief State Tracking (DST) problem of task-oriented conversational systems. Recent approaches to this problem leveraging Transformer-based models have yielded great results. However, training these models is expensive, both in terms of computational resources and time. Additionally, collecting high quality annotated dialogue datasets remains a challenge for researchers because of the extensive annotation requirement.

arxiv-2211-17082.title: Topological Frenkel Exciton-Polaritons in One-Dimensional Lattices of Strongly Coupled Cavities
arxiv-2211-17082.creator: J. Andrés Rojas-Sánchez, Yesenia A. García Jomaso, Brenda Vargas, David Ley Dominguez, César L. Ordoñez-Romero, Hugo A. Lara-García, Arturo Camacho-Guardian, Giuseppe Pirruccio
arxiv-2211-17082.description: Abstract Frenkel polaritons, hybrid light-matter quasiparticles, offer promises for the designing of new opto-electronic devices. However, their technological implementations are hindered by sensitivity to imperfections. Topology has raised as a way to circumvent defects and fabrication limitations. Here, we propose a lattice of cavities to realize the one-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model (SSH) for topological Frenkel polaritons.

arxiv-2307-05113.title: Piecing Together Clues: A Benchmark for Evaluating the Detective Skills of Large Language Models
arxiv-2307-05113.creator: Zhouhong Gu, Lin Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Haoning Ye, Xiaoxuan Zhu, Zihan Li, Zheyu Ye, Yan Gao, Yao Hu, Yanghua Xiao, Hongwei Feng
arxiv-2307-05113.description: Abstract Detectives frequently engage in information detection and reasoning simultaneously when making decisions across various cases, especially when confronted with a vast amount of information. With the rapid development of large language models (LLMs), evaluating how these models identify key information and reason to solve questions becomes increasingly relevant.

arxiv-2311-00106.title: Variational principle for a damped, quadratically interacting particle chain with nonconservative forcing
arxiv-2311-00106.creator: Amit Acharya Ambar N. Sengupta
arxiv-2311-00106.description: Abstract A method for designing variational principles for the dynamics of a possibly dissipative and non-conservatively forced chain of particles is demonstrated. Some qualitative features of the formulation are discussed. 1 Introduction Starting from the work of Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou [ 5 ] , much has been understood about non-generic, non-thermalized behavior in the mechanics of discrete particle chains, e.g.

arxiv-2402-14269.title: Optimal Mechanism in a Dynamic Stochastic Knapsack Environment
arxiv-2402-14269.creator: Jihyeok Jung, Chan-Oi Song, Deok-Joo Lee, Kiho Yoon
arxiv-2402-14269.description: Abstract This study introduces an optimal mechanism in a dynamic stochastic knapsack environment. The model features a single seller who has a fixed quantity of a perfectly divisible item. Impatient buyers with a piece-wise linear utility function arrive randomly and they report the two-dimensional private information: marginal value and demanded quantity.

arxiv-2404-12809.title: Mapping the SMEFT at High-Energy Colliders: from LEP and the (HL-)LHC to the FCC-ee
arxiv-2404-12809.creator: Eugenia Celada, Tommaso Giani, Jaco ter Hoeve, Luca Mantani, Juan Rojo, Alejo N. Rossia, Marion O. A. Thomas, and Eleni Vryonidou
arxiv-2404-12809.description: Abstract We present SMEFiT3.0 , an updated global SMEFT analysis of Higgs, top quark, and diboson production data from the LHC complemented by electroweak precision observables (EWPOs) from LEP and SLD. We consider recent inclusive and differential measurements from the LHC Run II, alongside with a novel implementation of the EWPOs based on independent calculations of the relevant EFT contributions.

arxiv-2508-00160.title: DeformTune: A Deformable XAI Music Prototype for Non-Musicians DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Explainable AI for the Arts Workshop 2025; June 23, 2025; Online ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06
arxiv-2508-00160.creator: Ziqing Xu, Nick Bryan-Kinns
arxiv-2508-00160.description: Abstract . Many existing AI music generation tools rely on text prompts, complex interfaces, or instrument-like controls, which may require musical or technical knowledge that non-musicians do not possess. This paper introduces DeformTune, a prototype system that combines a tactile deformable interface with the MeasureVAE model to explore more intuitive, embodied, and explainable AI interaction.

pmc-10648989.title: Active and Intelligent Packaging: A Review of the Possible Application of Cyclodextrins in Food Storage and Safety Indicators
pmc-10648989.creator: Andrés Leobardo Puebla-Duarte, Irela Santos-Sauceda, Francisco Rodríguez-Félix, Rey David Iturralde-García, Daniel Fernández-Quiroz, Ingrid Daniela Pérez-Cabral, Carmen Lizette Del-Toro-Sánchez, Jean-Marie Raquez, Andrea Ehrmann
pmc-10648989.description: Natural cyclodextrins (CDs) can be formed by 6, 7, or 8 glucose molecules (α-, β-, and γ-, respectively) linked in a ring, creating a cone shape. Its interior has an affinity for hydrophobic molecules, while the exterior is hydrophilic and can interact with water molecules.

pmc-12615259.title: Annotating the genome at single-nucleotide resolution with DNA foundation models
pmc-12615259.creator: Bernardo P. de Almeida, Hugo Dalla-Torre, Guillaume Richard, Christopher Blum, Lorenz Hexemer, Maxence Gélard, Javier Mendoza-Revilla, Ziqi Tang, Frederikke I. Marin, David M. Emms, Priyanka Pandey, Stefan Laurent, Marie Lopez, Alexandre Laterre, Maren Lang, Uğur Şahin, Karim Beguir, Thomas Pierrot
pmc-12615259.description: Genome annotation models that directly analyze DNA sequences are indispensable for modern biological research, enabling rapid and accurate identification of genes and other functional elements. Current annotation tools are typically developed for specific element classes and trained from scratch using supervised learning on datasets that are often limited in size.

pmc-13122914.title: Comparison of acetone and sodium phosphotungstic acid precipitation for sample enrichment prior to RT-QuIC for the detection of prion disease
pmc-13122914.creator: Eric M. Nicholson, Susan E. Veneziano
pmc-13122914.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Transmissible spongiform encephalopathies, or prion diseases, are fatal neurodegenerative diseases that are medically, economically, and ecologically important. In livestock and wildlife, detection to prevent introduction into a new herd or to assess environmental contamination is imperative for disease management. Real time quaking induced conversion (RT-QuIC) is an amplification-based approach with higher sensitivity than traditionally used immunoassays for TSEs and has been used to detect the presence of disease associated prions from various sample types.

pmc-13145979.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A260 STROKE DURING PREGNANCY AND THE POSTPARTUM PERIOD: A NATIONWIDE POPULATION-BASED STUDY IN SOUTH KOREA
pmc-13145979.creator: Cindy Yoon, Darda Chung
pmc-13145979.description: Background and aimsPregnancy-associated stroke (PAS) is a rare but clinically important complication of pregnancy. Despite its clinical significance, nationwide data on PAS are lacking in South Korea, a representative country with advanced maternal age. This study aimed to investigate the incidence, temporal trends, and risk factors of PAS in South Korea.

pmc-13528758.title: Fall Risk Identification with Innovative Technologies for Aging in Place: A Clinical Needs Assessment Study
pmc-13528758.creator: Titilola Yakubu, Nooshin Jafari, Michael Lim, Jamie Lam, Michelle Lin, Di Jiang, Kendall Ho
pmc-13528758.description: BackgroundFalls are a leading cause of injury and loss of independence among older adults. While gait-monitoring technologies offer promise for early fall risk detection, adoption is hindered by usability, cost, and integration challenges. Few studies incorporate perspectives from both patients and providers to inform user-centred design.

pmc-13536025.title: Nurse-led care model to overcome migration-related language barriers in people with cancer (IntVeM): study protocol for a controlled before-and-after study, process and economic evaluation
pmc-13536025.creator: Carolin Höckelmann, Johannes Bösche, Richard Dano, Stefanie Federhen, Annika Dangendorf, Wiebke Müller, Anne Adams, Kübra Annac, Yüce Yilmaz-Aslan, Patrick Brzoska, Minh Hai Vu, Sascha Köpke
pmc-13536025.description: IntroductionIn 2024, 30.4% of the German population had a migration background. People with migration-related language barriers face numerous challenges within the healthcare system, which can negatively impact their health outcomes. While language barriers affect healthcare in general, oncology represents a complex field in which effective communication is crucial.

pmc-13680003.title: Position Statement by the Saudi Heart Failure Working Group of the Saudi Heart Association on the Management of Advanced Heart Failure in Saudi Arabia
pmc-13680003.creator: Ibrahim Jelaidan, Abeer Bakhsh, Ammar G. Chaudhary, Ebtisam Alkhattaby, Fahmi AlKaf, Feras Khaliel, Ismail Raslan, Mohammed Alreshidan, Mosaad Alhussein, Waleed Alhabeeb
pmc-13680003.description: BackgroundHeart failure (HF) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in Saudi Arabia. Despite remarkable progress in guideline-directed medical therapy, a significant proportion of patients progress to advanced HF and require evaluation for heart transplantation or mechanical circulatory support (MCS).

uslaw-usc-t25-s1913.title: 25 U.S.C. § 1913 — Parental rights; voluntary termination
uslaw-usc-t25-s1913.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t25-s1913.description: United States Code, Title 25 (Indians); Chapter 21 (Indian Child Welfare); Subchapter I (Child Custody Proceedings). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Consent; record; certification matters; invalid consents Where any parent or Indian custodian voluntarily consents to a foster care placement or to termination of parental rights, such consent shall not be valid unless executed in writing and recorded before a judge.
